disclosure_text: I am an immigrant that came from Vietnam. I have lived in the US for 31 years.
micronarrative: What stands out to me first is the reaction of the local figure. What resonates with me personally is the coalition of neighborhood residents doing a "buy-out." That's a very cool act. I would have joined to buy the pastries as well if this happened in my local community. Last weekend, there was a peaceful protest about immigration in my community while I was driving by. I thought it was very interesting. The specific language or slogans were appropriate; it's just a reminder that our country was built based on immigrations. It is very similar compared to the everyday speech I hear in my neighborhood. The economic realities of local businesses like the bakery and shared linguistic familiarity are very much the same: we should be free to express our opinions in a peaceful way. My own experience of being perceived by others influenced a great deal how I interpret the hostility directed at the bakery, and that is as long as we do is legal, it shouldn't bother others.
